assignmentHtml.task: Research DuckDB as an analytics serving candidate. Investigate: (1) architecture — embedded columnar OLAP, single-process library; (2) ingestion — reading Parquet/CSV/JSON directly, arrow, ODBC/JDBC; no streaming; (3) updates/deletes — limited ALTER TABLE UPDATE/DELETE support; append-only by design primarily; (4) joins — excellent join performance, vectorized; (5) multi-tenant isolation — NONE natively (embedded); must be built at application layer; (6) recovery — file-based persistence; (7) license — MIT; (8) version caveats. Position DuckDB correctly: it is suitable for embedded/local analytics, NOT a shared serving layer.
assignmentHtml.context: Evidence cutoff 2026-09-16. Open-source analytics platform investigation. Requirements include multi-tenant serving, real-time dashboards, erasure, recovery. Only OSS. Determine where DuckDB fits.
assignmentHtml.expected_output: Structured dossier for DuckDB with architecture, ingestion, updates/deletes, joins, isolation, recovery, license, version caveats, with source URLs.

answerHtml: DuckDB is an embedded, single-process, columnar-vectorized OLAP library designed for local/analytics use inside host applications — NOT a shared serving layer. It reads Parquet/CSV/JSON/Arrow directly, supports ODBC/JDBC clients, and offers ACID transactions with optimistic MVCC. Updates/Deletes exist but are secondary to appends; DELETE does not reclaim space until CHECKPOINT. Joins are excellent (100M-row joins in seconds, 3–5x over PostgreSQL on star schemas). Multi-tenant isolation is entirely absent natively — no user management, RBAC, or row-level security — isolation must be built at the application layer (e.g., separate .duckdb files per tenant). Recovery is file-based via WAL replay on restart. Licensed MIT (fully open-source, held by the non-profit DuckDB Foundation). Version caveats: storage formats differ across versions (v0.8 uses storage version 51; v1.x uses 64+); backward compatibility (newer reading older files) was introduced in v0.10 and is the goal going forward, but forward compatibility is best-effort only; explicit STORAGE_VERSION options (v1.2+) allow opting into newer incompatible features; Quack remote protocol for multi-process access is beta as of v1.5.2, expected stable in v2.0 (fall 2026). For requirements including multi-tenant serving, real-time dashboards, erasure, and recovery, DuckDB fits only as an embedded analytics compute layer; the serving/isolation/recovery guarantees must be supplied externally.

evidence.snippet: DuckDB does not run as a separate process, but completely embedded within a host process... no DBMS server software to install... columnar-vectorized query execution engine... processes data in vectors of 2048 values... inspired by MonetDB/X100... Morsel-driven parallelism.
evidence.supports: DuckDB architecture: embedded, single-process, columnar-vectorized OLAP, no server component

evidence.snippet: CSV files can be read using the read_csv function, JSON files can be read using the read_json function... DuckDB is automatically able to query Pandas DataFrame, Polars DataFrame, Arrow objects... read_parquet('example.parquet')... direct SQL access: SELECT * FROM 'example.parquet'.
evidence.supports: Ingestion: native direct reading of Parquet, CSV, JSON, and Arrow/Pandas/Polars objects without copying

evidence.snippet: The DuckDB Java (JDBC) client lets Java applications query DuckDB through the standard JDBC API, version 4.1... jdbc:duckdb:/tmp/my_database opens a persistent database... installed from Maven Central.
evidence.supports: JDBC client support confirmed; also ODBC 3.0 driver (duckdb.org/docs/lts/clients/odbc/overview.html) available for all OSes

evidence.snippet: High-frequency ingest with streaming semantics: DuckDB isn't a streaming system; consider Kafka + Flink/Spark + lake/warehouse sinks. Always-on, multi-tenant analytics for large teams: you'll want a governed warehouse/lakehouse for permissions, lineage, and concurrent workloads.
evidence.supports: DuckDB has no native streaming ingestion and is not designed for multi-tenant serving

evidence.snippet: Running DELETE does not mean space is reclaimed. In general, rows are only marked as deleted. DuckDB reclaims space upon performing a CHECKPOINT. VACUUM currently does not reclaim space.
evidence.supports: DELETE exists but is append-secondary; space reclamation requires explicit CHECKPOINT

evidence.snippet: DuckDB supports concurrency within a single process... multiple writer threads using MVCC and optimistic concurrency control... A conflict error occurs when two threads attempt to update or delete the same row simultaneously... For multi-process write access, DuckDB's Quack remote protocol turns DuckDB into a client-server database (beta as of v1.5.2)... expected to become mature by v2.0 in fall 2026.
evidence.supports: Updates/Deletes supported with optimistic concurrency; multi-process write requires beta Quack protocol; no native multi-tenant isolation

evidence.snippet: DuckDB completed a 100M-row join in seconds, where SQLite and PostgreSQL lagged significantly behind. On fact-dimension star schema workloads, DuckDB consistently beat PostgreSQL by 3–5x.
evidence.supports: Excellent join performance: vectorized joins at scale, 3–5x faster than PostgreSQL on analytical star schemas

evidence.snippet: If your DuckDB session was writing to a persistent database file prior to crashing, there might be a WAL file next to your database named database_filename.wal. To recover data from the WAL file, simply start a new DuckDB session on the persistent database. DuckDB will then replay the write-ahead log and perform a checkpoint operation, restoring the database to the state before the crash.
evidence.supports: Recovery: file-based persistence with WAL replay on restart; automatic crash recovery

evidence.snippet: database_filename.wal — Write-ahead log file. If DuckDB exits normally, the WAL file is deleted upon exit. If DuckDB crashes, the WAL file is required to recover data.
evidence.supports: WAL behavior: deleted on normal exit, retained after crash for recovery

evidence.snippet: DuckDB is fully open-source under the MIT license... All components of DuckDB are available in the free version under this license: there is no 'enterprise version' of DuckDB. The DuckDB Foundation's statutes also ensure DuckDB remains open-source under the MIT license in perpetuity.
evidence.supports: MIT license, fully open-source, no enterprise tier, IP held by non-profit foundation

evidence.snippet: Backward compatibility refers to the ability of a newer DuckDB version to read storage files created by an older DuckDB version. Version 0.10 is the first release of DuckDB that supports backward compatibility... Forward compatibility is provided on a best effort basis... Default storage version for v1.0 to v1.5 is 64... STORAGE_VERSION option (v1.2+) allows explicitly specifying the storage version... files written with this option cannot be opened by older released versions.
evidence.supports: Version caveats: storage format changed across versions (51 for v0.8, 64+ for v1.x); backward compat since v0.10; forward compat best-effort; STORAGE_VERSION opt-in breaks compatibility with older versions

evidence.snippet: No sections on user management, RBAC, or row-level security found. Document covers sandboxing, prepared statements, resource limits, and safe mode only.
evidence.supports: No native multi-tenant isolation, no user management, no RBAC, no row-level security — isolation must be built at application layer
